List of default fields:[full_name, city, work_experience, roll_number, email_address, year_of_graduation, cgpa, univ, phone_number, contact_recruiter, branch, gender, degree, role, resume, pgdegree, city_graduation, gpa, major, linkedin]
For default fields add field in following way {predefined_label: 'roll_number', required: true} in the array.

If you want to add another field to candidate_details not present in default list, you can add in the following way:
{title: 'First Name', required: true, type: 'input'}. Following are the supported input types: [input, select, radio, checkbox, file]

In case of input being select, you can send options for select in following way: {title: 'Age', required: true, type: 'select', options: ['<20', '20-30', '>30']}

Order of candidate_details will be same as order of array

attempt_events.description:
List of events that occurred during the attempt. Each event contains fields: id, attempt_id,event (event type), data (event-specific data), inserttime (timestamp).

List of events:
1 - Logged in to the test
2 - Viewed question list
3 - Viewed question. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
4 - Submitted answer for question. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
5 - Code execution for question. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
6 - Ping to server
7 - Went invisible / Switched tab or window. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
8 - Went Visible / Switched back to test. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
9 - Text pasted from external source. Will get pasted_text, pasted_text_char_count, pasted_text_line_count, pasted_text_truncated, qid, qno fields in data.
10 - Rendered code for question

attempt_metrics.description: AI fluency data for the candidate's attempt as a whole. Opt-in via additional_fields=attempt_metrics.ai_fluency. Only present once the candidate's top-level status is 7 (completed); omitted entirely until then, even if requested. See AttemptMetric for the record shape.

items.description:
A metric record with a shared type, status, and metric_data shape. The attempt-level attempt_metrics field contains AI fluency; the per-question metrics array can contain AI fluency or code quality. The contents of metric_data depend on the metric type.

AI fluency is an evolving feature — data fields, rubric keys, and reasoning entry shapes may change as the evaluation model is improved.

ai_fluency_summary: The candidate demonstrated limited context quality, critical thinking, and collaboration. Thus, the overall AI fluency is limited with a grade of C.

reasoning.text: The candidate rarely built on the AI assistant's suggestions.

events.summary: submitted immediately after receiving file guidance, with zero edits to any file

reasoning.text: The candidate provided clear error messages and code context in most prompts.
The candidate relied on the AI assistant before attempting an independent approach.

metric_data.description:
Present only when status is "available". Fields:

ai_fluency_grade (string) — Overall grade: A, B, C, or NA. Absent on older records that predate grading — those records contain only ai_fluency_summary.

ai_fluency_summary (array of strings) — Human-readable summary sentences describing the candidate's AI usage. Always present.

rubrics (object) — Per-rubric breakdown, keyed by rubric name (presently collaboration, context_quality, critical_thinking). Absent whenever ai_fluency_grade is absent or is NA. Each rubric contains:

  grade (string) — Same enum as ai_fluency_grade.

  reasoning (array) — Ordered entries explaining the grade, typically one text entry followed by one or more citation entries. Each entry has a type field — one of:

    type: "text" — Natural-language summary of the rubric grade.
      - text — the explanation string.

    type: "citation" — Grouped evidence from the candidate's session. Contains a data array; each group has:
      - key — short label for the evidence group.
      - messages (optional) — chat-transcript evidence. Each entry has text (verbatim message sent to the AI assistant), message_id, and question_id.
      - events (optional) — session events performed by the candidate (e.g. submission_attempted, suggestion_decision). Each entry has offset, summary, event_id, and event_type. question_id is present at the attempt level (aggregating multiple questions); omitted at the per-question level where it would be redundant.
      A group may carry messages, events, or both.

Code quality metric_data:

status (string) — Report processing status: success, in progress, failed, or not generated.

processed (boolean) — Whether report processing has finished.

report (object) — Filtered code quality report; present on success.

grade (string or null) — A, B, or C on success; - if a successful report has no grade; not generated when the report was not generated; null while in progress.

status.description: "available" when metric_data is present, or "not_applicable" when no usable metric data is available (the metric_data field is omitted). For code quality, metric_data.status separately describes report processing and may be "in progress", "failed", or another report status.

type.description: Metric type. Known values are "ai_fluency" and "code_quality"; attempt-level metrics currently contain only "ai_fluency".

attempt_starttime.description: Time at which candidate started the test. This will be null if candidate has not attempted the test yet.

authenticated_report_url.description: URL for candidate report that is accessible to all users in your HackerRank account.

comments.description:
All the comments left on the summary tab of the report.
For comments left on individual questions, expand questions field too.

editor_paste_count.description: when track_editor_paste is enabled for the test, this field returns the number of times this candidate pasted a piece of code.

evaluator_email.description: Email address of the evaluator, if different from the test admins and owner.

feedback.description: Feedback given by the candidate at the end of the test.

integrity_status.description: Consolidated view of all integrity-related signals for an attempt. Possible values: "High" (high risk), "Medium" (medium risk), "No Issues Detected" (no integrity issues found), nil (not evaluated)

integrity_summary.description: Detailed text summary of integrity-related signals for an attempt. Contains formatted text describing specific integrity issues detected (e.g., tab switches, code similarity, secure mode violations). null if not evaluated

invite_email_done.description: Whether an invite email has been sent to candidate or not.

invite_link.description: Invite test link for the candidate.

invite_metadata.description: Customizable metadata that can be set for a candidate. This must be a valid JSON object.

invite_valid.description: Whether this invite is still valid or not.

invite_valid_from.description: Time from when invite for this test candidate is valid. Null value in this field indicates that invite is permanently valid.

invite_valid_to.description: Time till when invite for this test candidate is valid. Null value in this field indicates that invite is permanently valid.

invited_on.description: Timestamp of when candidate was invited for the test.

max_code_similarity.description: [DEPRECATED] This gives the question level measure of candidate's code similarity. Candidate's code is compared with that of other candidates for the specific question. Maximum similarity percentage at the time of test submission is returned. This field is deprecated. Please use integrity_status and integrity_summary instead.

out_of_window_duration.description: When candidate_tab_switch is enabled for the test, this field returns the number of seconds this candidate went out of window.

out_of_window_events.description: When candidate_tab_switch is enabled for the test, this field returns the number of times this candidate went out of window.

pdf_url.description: URL for a PDF version of the candidate report.

percentage_score.description: Percentage score of the candidate for the test.

performance_summary.description:
Performance summary of the candidates,
including details about the candidates test results and AI-generated summaries.

plagiarism.description: [DEPRECATED] Question wise details of plagiarism. This field is deprecated. Please use integrity_status and integrity_summary instead.

plagiarism_status.description: [DEPRECATED] Whether this candidate has been flagged as plagiarized or not. This field is deprecated. Please use integrity_status and integrity_summary instead.

proctor_images.description: When enable_proctoring is enabled for the test, this field returns a list of urls that contains the images of this candidate taken during the test.

questions.description:
Question wise score split for this candidate in this attempt.
List of fields when questions is expanded:[answered, answers, score, plagiarism, name, preview, type, max_score, comments]

plagiarism is an object and has the fields [solve_id, test_candidate_id, email, similarity]

comments gives the comments left on the report for the given question (you need to also pass comments in additional fields for this)

Additional fields
Additional fields can be passed as csv for query parameter additional_fields
ex: additional_fields=questions.time_taken

Additional fields supported in response:
[time_taken, submissions, submission_result, plagiarism_details, total_typing_time, time_to_start_typing, initial_repo, solution_zip, scoring_output, code_diff, ai_transcript, ide_signals, ai_fluency, code_quality]

time_taken gives the time taken per question by the candidate. Accessed by questions.time_taken

submissions gives the list of all submissions done by the candidate for the given question. Accessed by questions.solves

submission_result gives the detailed submission information for each testcase. Accessed by questions.submission_result

plagiarism_details gives plagiarism details for each question including suspicion_score, suspicion_category, max_code_similarity, suspicion_reason, potential_reference_taking time intervals. Accessed by questions.plagiarism_details

total_typing_time gives the total typing time for each question. Accessed by questions.total_typing_time

code_quality_grade code quality grade for each question questions.code_quality_grade

time_to_start_typing gives the time between question viewed and started typing for each question. Accessed by questions.time_to_start_typing

ai_fluency AI fluency data for this question, returned as a metrics array inside each question. Accessed by questions.ai_fluency. See AttemptMetric for the record shape.

code_quality Code quality status, grade, and filtered report in the metrics array. Accessed by questions.code_quality on the show candidate endpoint. Ignored by list and search.

Project-based (fullstack) question artifacts. Each is opt-in and returned only for fullstack questions:

initial_repo_url URL of the question starter repository zip. Accessed by questions.initial_repo

solution_zip_url gitlist zipball download link (with access view key) for the candidate final repository. Accessed by questions.solution_zip

scoring_output_url URL of the scoring output log. Accessed by questions.scoring_output

code_diff_url presigned URL of the candidate code diff. Accessed by questions.code_diff

ai_transcript_url presigned URL of the AI chat transcript. Accessed by questions.ai_transcript

ide_signals_url presigned URL of the IDE signals log. Unlike the other fields in this group, this is also returned for coderepo_task questions, not just fullstack. Accessed by questions.ide_signals

ide_signals_filename name of the jsonl file inside the ide_signals_url zip. It is ade-signals.jsonl or ide-signals.jsonl depending on the workspace mode the candidate ran in. Accessed by questions.ide_signals

candidate_details.description:
List of details that candidates will be asked to enter before logging into the test. These details will be available in the report view of the test. It should be an Array of JSON.

List of default fields:[full_name, city, work_experience, roll_number, email_address, year_of_graduation, cgpa, univ, phone_number, contact_recruiter, branch, gender, degree, role, resume, pgdegree, city_graduation, gpa, major, linkedin]
For default fields add field in following way {predefined_label: 'roll_number', required: true} in the array.

If you want to add another field to candidate_details not present in default list, you can add in the following way:
{title: 'First Name', required: true, type: 'input'}. Following are the supported input types: [input, select, radio, checkbox, file]

In case of input being select, you can send options for select in following way: {title: 'Age', required: true, type: 'select', options: ['<20', '20-30', '>30']}

Order of candidate_details will be same as order of array

attempt_events.description:
List of events that occurred during the attempt. Each event contains fields: id, attempt_id,event (event type), data (event-specific data), inserttime (timestamp).

List of events:
1 - Logged in to the test
2 - Viewed question list
3 - Viewed question. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
4 - Submitted answer for question. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
5 - Code execution for question. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
6 - Ping to server
7 - Went invisible / Switched tab or window. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
8 - Went Visible / Switched back to test. Will get qid, qno, question_version fields in data.
9 - Text pasted from external source. Will get pasted_text, pasted_text_char_count, pasted_text_line_count, pasted_text_truncated, qid, qno fields in data.
10 - Rendered code for question

attempt_metrics.description: AI fluency data for the candidate's attempt as a whole. Opt-in via additional_fields=attempt_metrics.ai_fluency. Only present once the candidate's top-level status is 7 (completed); omitted entirely until then, even if requested. See AttemptMetric for the record shape.

items.description:
A metric record with a shared type, status, and metric_data shape. The attempt-level attempt_metrics field contains AI fluency; the per-question metrics array can contain AI fluency or code quality. The contents of metric_data depend on the metric type.

AI fluency is an evolving feature — data fields, rubric keys, and reasoning entry shapes may change as the evaluation model is improved.

ai_fluency_summary: The candidate demonstrated limited context quality, critical thinking, and collaboration. Thus, the overall AI fluency is limited with a grade of C.

reasoning.text: The candidate rarely built on the AI assistant's suggestions.

events.summary: submitted immediately after receiving file guidance, with zero edits to any file

reasoning.text: The candidate provided clear error messages and code context in most prompts.
The candidate relied on the AI assistant before attempting an independent approach.

metric_data.description:
Present only when status is "available". Fields:

ai_fluency_grade (string) — Overall grade: A, B, C, or NA. Absent on older records that predate grading — those records contain only ai_fluency_summary.

ai_fluency_summary (array of strings) — Human-readable summary sentences describing the candidate's AI usage. Always present.

rubrics (object) — Per-rubric breakdown, keyed by rubric name (presently collaboration, context_quality, critical_thinking). Absent whenever ai_fluency_grade is absent or is NA. Each rubric contains:

  grade (string) — Same enum as ai_fluency_grade.

  reasoning (array) — Ordered entries explaining the grade, typically one text entry followed by one or more citation entries. Each entry has a type field — one of:

    type: "text" — Natural-language summary of the rubric grade.
      - text — the explanation string.

    type: "citation" — Grouped evidence from the candidate's session. Contains a data array; each group has:
      - key — short label for the evidence group.
      - messages (optional) — chat-transcript evidence. Each entry has text (verbatim message sent to the AI assistant), message_id, and question_id.
      - events (optional) — session events performed by the candidate (e.g. submission_attempted, suggestion_decision). Each entry has offset, summary, event_id, and event_type. question_id is present at the attempt level (aggregating multiple questions); omitted at the per-question level where it would be redundant.
      A group may carry messages, events, or both.

Code quality metric_data:

status (string) — Report processing status: success, in progress, failed, or not generated.

processed (boolean) — Whether report processing has finished.

report (object) — Filtered code quality report; present on success.

grade (string or null) — A, B, or C on success; - if a successful report has no grade; not generated when the report was not generated; null while in progress.

status.description: "available" when metric_data is present, or "not_applicable" when no usable metric data is available (the metric_data field is omitted). For code quality, metric_data.status separately describes report processing and may be "in progress", "failed", or another report status.

type.description: Metric type. Known values are "ai_fluency" and "code_quality"; attempt-level metrics currently contain only "ai_fluency".

List of fields when questions is expanded:[answered, answers, score, plagiarism, name, preview, type, max_score, comments]

comments gives the comments left on the report for the given question (you need to also pass comments in additional fields for this)

Additional fields
Additional fields can be passed as csv for query parameter additional_fields
ex: additional_fields=questions.time_taken

[time_taken, submissions, submission_result, plagiarism_details, total_typing_time, time_to_start_typing, initial_repo, solution_zip, scoring_output, code_diff, ai_transcript, ide_signals, ai_fluency, code_quality]

time_taken gives the time taken per question by the candidate. Accessed by questions.time_taken

submissions gives the list of all submissions done by the candidate for the given question. Accessed by questions.solves

submission_result gives the detailed submission information for each testcase. Accessed by questions.submission_result

plagiarism_details gives plagiarism details for each question including suspicion_score, suspicion_category, max_code_similarity, suspicion_reason, potential_reference_taking time intervals. Accessed by questions.plagiarism_details

total_typing_time gives the total typing time for each question. Accessed by questions.total_typing_time

code_quality_grade code quality grade for each question questions.code_quality_grade

time_to_start_typing gives the time between question viewed and started typing for each question. Accessed by questions.time_to_start_typing

ai_fluency AI fluency data for this question, returned as a metrics array inside each question. Accessed by questions.ai_fluency. See AttemptMetric for the record shape.

Project-based (fullstack) question artifacts. Each is opt-in and returned only for fullstack questions:

initial_repo_url URL of the question starter repository zip. Accessed by questions.initial_repo

solution_zip_url gitlist zipball download link (with access view key) for the candidate final repository. Accessed by questions.solution_zip

scoring_output_url URL of the scoring output log. Accessed by questions.scoring_output

code_diff_url presigned URL of the candidate code diff. Accessed by questions.code_diff

ai_transcript_url presigned URL of the AI chat transcript. Accessed by questions.ai_transcript

ide_signals_url presigned URL of the IDE signals log. Unlike the other fields in this group, this is also returned for coderepo_task questions, not just fullstack. Accessed by questions.ide_signals

ide_signals_filename name of the jsonl file inside the ide_signals_url zip. It is ade-signals.jsonl or ide-signals.jsonl depending on the workspace mode the candidate ran in. Accessed by questions.ide_signals

report_url.description: URL for candidate report that is accessible only to HackerRank users with access to the specific test.

score.description: Score of the candidate if they have attempted the test.

scores_skills_split.description: Score of candidate split per skill.

scores_tags_split.description: Score of candidate split per tag.

secure_mode_exit_count.description: When enable_secure_assessment_mode is enabled for the test, this field returns the number of times this candidate exited secure/fullscreen mode.

secure_mode_exit_duration.description: When enable_secure_assessment_mode is enabled for the test, this field returns the total number of seconds this candidate spent outside secure/fullscreen mode.

status.description: This indicates the current status of the candidate. Can be between -1 to 7. -1 indicates that candidate is currently invited, while 7 indicates that candidates has completed the test and a report has been generated for the candidate. All other intermediate states are internal and should not be used.

tags.description: List of tags associated with this candidate.

test_finish_url.description: Candidate will be redirected to this URL when the test gets over. By default, they are sent to the feedback page.

test_result_url.description: Webhook URL for candidate report. When the report is processed the report data will be sent to this URL as a webhook. By default, the inviter will get the report by email.

unclaimed_added_time.description: Unclaimed added time for this candidate.

next.description: URL for next page. This will be empty when current page is last page

page_total.description: Count of total candidates in current page

previous.description: URL for previous page. This will be empty when current page is first page

candidate_details.description:
List of details that candidates will be asked to enter before logging into the test. These details will be available in the report view of the test. It should be an Array of JSON.

List of default fields:[full_name, city, work_experience, roll_number, email_address, year_of_graduation, cgpa, univ, phone_number, contact_recruiter, branch, gender, degree, role, resume, pgdegree, city_graduation, gpa, major, linkedin]
For default fields add field in following way {predefined_label: 'roll_number', required: true} in the array.

If you want to add another field to candidate_details not present in default list, you can add in the following way:
{title: 'First Name', required: true, type: 'input'}. Following are the supported input types: [input, select, radio, checkbox, file]

In case of input being select, you can send options for select in following way: {title: 'Age', required: true, type: 'select', options: ['<20', '20-30', '>30']}

Order of candidate_details will be same as order of array

created_at.description: Timestamp when this test was created

custom_acknowledge_text.default: I will not consult/copy code from any source including a website, book, or friend/colleague to complete these tests, though may refer language documentation or use an IDE that has code completion features.
custom_acknowledge_text.description: Candidate will be asked to agree to this text before logging into the test.

cutoff_score.description: If set, then candidates scoring equal or more than this value will automatically be placed into "Qualified" bucket, while candidates scoring less will be placed in "Failed" bucket

draft.description: Describes if this test is currently in Draft(true)/Published(false) state. Candidates can only be invited for published tests.

enable_acknowledgement.description: If set to false, then candidate will not be asked to agree to acknowledgement text.

enable_advanced_proctoring.description:
If set to true, candidate webcam photos are analyzed using AI to detect suspicious activity.We will take snapshots periodically during the Test, and you can view them in the Candidate's report.This corresponds to Image analysis setting under Integrity settings of a test
By default this field is set to false.

enable_ml_plagiarism_analysis.description:
If set to true, this detects whether a candidate has received help from an external source.This corresponds to AI Plagiarism setting under Integrity settings of a test
By default this field is set to false.

enable_photo_identification.description:
If set to true, this requires candidates to take a photo before starting the test.This corresponds to Photo Identification setting under Integrity settings of a test
By default this field is set to false.

enable_proctoring.description:
If set to true, then this will force the candidate to turn their webcam on before starting the Test.We will take snapshots periodically during the Test, and you can view them in the Candidate's report.This corresponds to Image Proctoring setting under Integrity settings of a test
By default this field is set to false.

enable_secure_assessment_mode.description:
If set to true, then this will enable secure mode for the test.This corresponds to Secure mode setting under Integrity settings of a test
By default this field is set to false.

endtime.description: If set, then logins after this time will be disabled. Candidates who are already logged in will be able to give the test normally even after endtime.

experience.description: Experience levels associated with this test.

hide_compile_test.description: If set to true then candidate will not be able to see compile button for coding and approximate type questions.

hide_template.description: If set to true then head and tail templates will not be shown to candidates.
